sekcje.tresc:
OBJECTIVE 1: EMPOWER YOUTH WITH FEWER OPPORTUNITIES AS DIGITAL INCLUSION TRAINERS

DIGI-BRIDGE will train 40 young people with fewer opportunities (NEETs, rural residents, migrants aged 18-29) from NEF's Young AI Explorers and E-Senior programs in Poland and CKM's ACTIV8! and Youth for Society programs in Croatia as certified Digital Bridge Trainers by month 12. This objective directly addresses the Inclusion and Diversity priority by transforming disadvantaged youth from passive service recipients into active agents of digital inclusion.

Rationale: According to Eurostat (2024), 23% of youth in transformation regions face NEET status, lacking purpose and meaningful engagement. Our reverse mentoring methodology transforms this: youth gain teaching skills and professional competencies while contributing to intergenerational solidarity.

Expected outcome: 40 certified Digital Bridge Trainers, 80-page Training Toolkit in three languages (PL, HR, EN), and a multiplier pool ready to scale the methodology.

KPIs: 90% completion rate, 80% satisfaction score, 70% report increased sense of purpose (pre/post survey).

OBJECTIVE 2: INCREASE DIGITAL COMPETENCE OF ISOLATED SENIORS

The project will increase digital competence of 40 seniors aged 65+ by minimum 50% (DigComp framework scores) by month 15. Participants come from CKM's 'Za njihovu dobrobit' home care database (120 beneficiaries) and NEF's 'Google for Seniors' alumni (160 trained).

Rationale: Eurostat (2024) reports 42% of Polish and 54% of Croatian seniors lack basic digital skills. WHO (2023) documented 35% increase in post-COVID social isolation among elderly. Digital exclusion compounds social exclusion - our objective addresses both barriers simultaneously.

Expected outcome: 40 seniors with Digital Citizen certificates demonstrating proficiency in 5 essential tasks: video calling, online health services, digital banking, social groups, and voice assistants.

KPIs: DigComp score +50% (pre/post assessment), Social Connection Index +40%, 85% perform 5 digital tasks independently.

OBJECTIVE 3: DEPLOY AI-POWERED ACCESSIBILITY TOOL FOR SUSTAINED INCLUSION

Develop and deploy 'DigiMost' AI Voice Assistant with 500+ user interactions by month 15. This voice-first, multilingual (PL, HR, EN) tool addresses accessibility gaps in existing digital education resources.

Rationale: Current tools require screen literacy, mouse navigation, and reading proficiency - barriers for seniors. Our assistant uses natural voice interaction and simplified commands designed for first-time users.

Expected outcome: Open-source AI Voice Assistant providing 24/7 accessible digital support beyond project activities.

KPIs: 500+ logged interactions, 4.0/5.0 satisfaction rating, 80% weekly assistant usage during pilot.

PRIORITY ALIGNMENT: All objectives address Inclusion and Diversity through targeting disadvantaged groups (NEETs, isolated seniors, rural populations), removing participation barriers (voice-first AI, intergenerational support), and promoting cross-generational solidarity. Digital Transformation is addressed via AI development; Participation through youth activation and seniors' community reconnection.

PRIMARY TARGET GROUP: YOUTH WITH FEWER OPPORTUNITIES (40 participants)

Profile: Young people aged 18-29 facing multiple barriers to social inclusion:
- 20 participants from NEF programs in Silesian Voivodeship, Poland: alumni of 'Young AI Explorers' digital skills program and 'E-Senior' intergenerational initiative, including NEETs from post-industrial communities, rural youth from Zawiercie region, and young migrants participating in integration programs
- 20 participants from CKM programs in Dubrovnik-Neretva County, Croatia: beneficiaries of 'ACTIV8!' youth activation project and 'Youth for Society' civic engagement program, including island community youth facing geographical isolation, young unemployed from tourism-dependent economy, and youth from minority backgrounds

Identified needs (based on needs assessment conducted by both organizations):
- 78% lack meaningful engagement opportunities that connect them to older generations (NEF survey, N=45, 2024)
- 65% express desire for skill development that leads to concrete community contribution (CKM focus groups, 2024)
- Limited access to structured mentoring and professional development in non-formal education sector
- Social disconnection exacerbated by digital communication patterns replacing face-to-face intergenerational contact

How project addresses needs: Youth become certified Digital Bridge Trainers through 5-day intensive course, gaining pedagogical skills, AI literacy, and structured mentoring experience. The reverse mentoring model transforms them from passive beneficiaries to active contributors, building confidence and employability skills.

SECONDARY TARGET GROUP: DIGITALLY EXCLUDED SENIORS (40 participants)

Profile: Adults aged 65+ experiencing digital exclusion and social isolation:
- 20 seniors from CKM's 'Za njihovu dobrobit' (For Their Well-being) home care program database of 120 beneficiaries in Dubrovnik area, primarily living alone with limited family contact, receiving regular home visits from CKM volunteers
- 20 seniors from NEF's 'Google for Seniors' alumni network of 160 graduates in Silesian region, who completed basic digital literacy but need continued support and advanced skills

Identified needs (based on organization records and participant feedback):
- 54% of Croatian and 42% of Polish seniors lack basic digital skills (Eurostat 2024)
- 67% of CKM's home care beneficiaries report feeling isolated, with digital exclusion compounding social exclusion (program records, 2024)
- Need for patient, personalized digital support that respects their pace and addresses specific practical needs (banking, healthcare, family communication)
- Desire for meaningful intergenerational connection, not just technical training

How project addresses needs: Seniors receive personalized 10-week training (2h/week) from youth trainers in pairs, supported by AI Voice Assistant for 24/7 help. Focus on 5 practical skills: video calling family, accessing health services, digital banking, joining social groups online, and using voice assistants.

INDIRECT BENEFICIARIES: YOUTH WORKERS AND WIDER COMMUNITY (80+ people)

- 20 youth workers and trainers from both organizations who will be trained as multipliers, integrating the methodology into their regular work
- Family members of participating seniors (estimated 80 people) who benefit from improved digital communication with their elderly relatives
- Local communities in Zawiercie and Dubrovnik regions through public multiplier events (100 participants)

sekcje.tresc:
THE CHALLENGE: CONVERGING CRISES OF DIGITAL EXCLUSION AND SOCIAL ISOLATION

Europe faces a demographic and digital double challenge. By 2030, one in four Europeans will be over 65 (Eurostat population projections), yet digital transformation accelerates without adequate inclusion measures. The COVID-19 pandemic exposed and deepened this divide: WHO (2023) reports 35% increase in social isolation among seniors, while essential services migrated online. Meanwhile, 23% of youth in transformation regions remain disconnected from meaningful engagement (NEET status, Eurostat 2024).

Specific regional context amplifies urgency:
- In Silesian Voivodeship (Poland), post-industrial transition leaves both generations struggling: seniors lose community networks, youth lack employment pathways
- In Dubrovnik-Neretva County (Croatia), tourism-dependent economy creates seasonal precarity for youth while island isolation compounds senior loneliness
- Both regions show above-EU-average rates of digital exclusion among 65+ populations (42% Poland, 54% Croatia vs. 37% EU average)

INNOVATION GAP: WHY EXISTING SOLUTIONS FAIL

Current digital inclusion programs treat seniors as passive recipients of technical training, ignoring the social dimension of digital exclusion. They fail because:
1. One-way teaching ignores seniors' life experience and contribution potential
2. Standard interfaces assume screen literacy, mouse navigation, and reading proficiency
3. One-time training without ongoing support leads to skill decay
4. Youth involvement limited to service delivery, not mutual learning

DIGI-BRIDGE addresses these gaps through three innovations: (a) reverse mentoring model where youth teach digital skills while seniors provide life wisdom mentoring, creating mutual value and sustained relationships; (b) AI Voice Assistant 'DigiMost' providing 24/7 accessible support through voice-first interaction, eliminating traditional interface barriers; (c) intergenerational pair model ensuring personalized, patient, relationship-based learning rather than classroom instruction.

TIMING: WHY THIS PROJECT, WHY NOW

Three converging developments make 2026 the optimal moment:
1. AI accessibility breakthrough: Large language models now enable natural voice interaction at low cost, making previously expensive assistive technology feasible for small-scale projects
2. Post-pandemic awareness: Both organizations observed increased demand from seniors seeking digital connection and youth seeking meaningful engagement after COVID isolation
3. Policy alignment: EU Digital Decade targets (80% basic digital skills by 2030) and European Pillar of Social Rights (active ageing, intergenerational solidarity) directly support this intervention

WHY ERASMUS+ FUNDING IS ESSENTIAL

This project requires Erasmus+ support because:
1. Transnational cooperation is core to the innovation: Polish AI expertise (NEF) combined with Croatian intergenerational methodology (CKM) creates a solution neither could develop alone
2. Scale and replicability: EU funding enables development of multilingual tools and open-access methodology transferable across Europe
3. Youth mobility dimension: Training course brings Polish and Croatian youth together, building European identity through shared purpose
4. No alternative funding: National programs focus on either digital skills OR intergenerational work, not their intersection. Private sector has no incentive for senior-focused accessibility tools. Only Erasmus+ KA210 supports this exact combination of youth work, digital inclusion, and transnational partnership.

sekcje.tresc:
ADDRESSING TARGET GROUP NEEDS THROUGH INTEGRATED METHODOLOGY

DIGI-BRIDGE employs a three-pillar methodology designed to address the specific needs identified in our target group analysis:

PILLAR 1: REVERSE MENTORING MODEL
Addressing youth need for meaningful engagement and senior need for personalized support

Traditional digital training treats seniors as passive learners and youth as service providers. Our reverse mentoring model inverts this: youth teach digital skills while seniors share life experience and wisdom. This addresses:
- Youth need for purpose: 78% of surveyed NEF participants lacked meaningful intergenerational engagement. As Digital Bridge Trainers, they become agents of change, not service recipients
- Senior need for respect: Instead of infantilizing 'help for the elderly,' seniors contribute actively through mentoring youth on professional skills, life decisions, and community knowledge
- Relationship sustainability: Pairs continue beyond formal training, creating lasting intergenerational bonds

Implementation: Youth undergo 5-day Training Course (Activity 2) learning pedagogical techniques, patience strategies, and AI tool operation. They then deliver 10-week pilot sessions (Activity 3) meeting seniors 2 hours weekly, alternating digital training with reverse mentoring conversations.

PILLAR 2: AI VOICE ASSISTANT 'DIGIMOST'
Addressing senior need for accessible, 24/7 support and youth need for scalable tools

Seniors identified key barriers: 'I forget what we learned between sessions,' 'I'm afraid to try alone and break something,' 'I can't read small text on screens.' DigiMost AI addresses each:
- Voice-first interaction: No mouse, keyboard, or screen reading required. Seniors speak naturally: 'DigiMost, how do I video call my daughter?'
- 24/7 availability: Support between training sessions when youth trainers unavailable
- Multilingual: Polish, Croatian, and English for diverse communities and family abroad
- Error tolerance: Reassuring, patient responses encouraging experimentation

Implementation: NEF's AI specialist Anton Luzan leads development (Activity 4) using open-source language models. Testing integrated into pilot sessions with iterative improvement based on senior feedback.

PILLAR 3: STRUCTURED INTERGENERATIONAL PAIRING
Addressing organizational goal of sustainable methodology and participant need for personalization

Random group training fails seniors who need individual attention. Our pair model ensures:
- Personalized pace: Each senior works with dedicated youth trainer who adapts to their learning speed
- Accountability: Fixed pairs create mutual commitment and relationship investment
- Practical focus: Training covers five skills seniors identified as priority: video calling family, accessing healthcare online, digital banking basics, joining social groups, operating voice assistants
- Progress tracking: Both partners complete pre/post assessments using DigComp framework and Social Connection Index

ADDRESSING ORGANIZATIONAL GOALS

For New Europe Foundation (NEF):
- Expands 'Google for Seniors' program with AI-powered tools and methodology
- Develops team expertise in AI accessibility applications
- Strengthens youth work portfolio with intergenerational component
- Creates replicable model for Erasmus+ Accreditation activities (2024-2028)

For Youth Career Center Dubrovnik (CKM):
- Advances 'Za njihovu dobrobit' program with digital inclusion dimension
- Develops staff competencies in AI-assisted learning
- Expands youth engagement beyond traditional career guidance
- Generates transferable toolkit for other Croatian youth organizations

Both organizations gain: European partnership experience, open-access outputs for continued use, trained multipliers for methodology scaling, and documented impact data supporting future funding applications.

sekcje.tresc:
WHY POLISH-CROATIAN PARTNERSHIP IS ESSENTIAL

DIGI-BRIDGE brings together two organizations with complementary expertise that neither could achieve alone. This transnational cooperation is not administrative convenience but strategic necessity for creating a truly innovative and scalable solution.

COMPLEMENTARY EXPERTISE: TECHNOLOGY MEETS HUMAN CARE

New Europe Foundation (Poland) brings:
- AI development capacity: Staff AI specialist Anton Luzan with proven track record in chatbot development, GPT integration, and multilingual applications
- Digital seniors methodology: 'Google for Seniors' program successfully trained 160 seniors in basic digital literacy, providing tested pedagogical approaches
- Youth digital skills focus: 'Young AI Explorers' program developed curriculum for youth AI education
- Technical infrastructure: Server capacity, development environment, API integrations

Youth Career Center Dubrovnik (Croatia) brings:
- Intergenerational care expertise: 'Za njihovu dobrobit' projects (1M EUR budget, 120 senior beneficiaries) developed home-based care model with strong relational component
- Senior access network: Direct connection to isolated seniors through ongoing home visit program, trust relationships already established
- Youth activation methodology: ACTIV8! and Youth for Society programs engaged disadvantaged youth in community service
- Evaluation experience: Robust impact assessment frameworks from large-scale ESF projects

SYNERGY: 1+1=3

The partnership creates value exceeding sum of parts:
- NEF's AI cannot reach isolated seniors without CKM's trusted relationships
- CKM's care model cannot scale without NEF's technological tools
- Neither can develop multilingual, cross-cultural solution alone
- Together: AI accessibility + human connection = sustainable digital inclusion

KNOWLEDGE TRANSFER IN BOTH DIRECTIONS

Poland → Croatia:
- AI development skills transfer to CKM staff through joint development process
- Digital literacy teaching techniques from 'Google for Seniors' experience
- Technical documentation and code in open-source repository for CKM continued use

Croatia → Poland:
- Intergenerational care methodology from 'Za njihovu dobrobit' experience
- Senior outreach and trust-building techniques
- Impact evaluation frameworks and quality assurance processes

EU-WIDE SCALABILITY

Transnational design ensures European relevance:
- Multilingual outputs (Polish, Croatian, English) immediately usable in three language communities
- Cross-cultural testing: If methodology works in both Slavic contexts with different EU membership histories, adaptation to other countries is validated
- Open access: All outputs (toolkit, AI code, training materials) published under Creative Commons CC-BY license on E+ Results Platform
- Addressing common challenge: Digital exclusion among seniors and youth disengagement are EU-wide issues (Eurostat data confirms similar patterns across member states)

EUROPEAN IDENTITY BUILDING

Beyond practical outputs, transnational cooperation builds European citizenship:
- Training Course brings 40 Polish and Croatian youth together for 5 days, creating lasting cross-border friendships
- Joint problem-solving across languages demonstrates EU added value concretely
- Youth experience first-hand that European solutions work better than national isolation
- Both countries' EU membership stories (Poland 2004, Croatia 2013) provide intercultural learning about European integration journey

COMPARATIVE ADVANTAGE

Why not purely national project?
- Polish project alone: AI without care infrastructure, no access to isolated seniors
- Croatian project alone: Care model without technological innovation, limited digital expertise
- Transnational project: Complete solution combining technology, methodology, and scale

This partnership represents unique value proposition: the only combination in Europe of proven AI accessibility development (NEF) with established intergenerational home care network (CKM). This competitive advantage would disappear in national-only implementation.

DIGI-BRIDGE systematically addresses all four Erasmus+ horizontal priorities through concrete measures integrated throughout project design and implementation.

1. INCLUSION AND DIVERSITY

DIGI-BRIDGE places inclusion at its core, targeting populations facing multiple barriers to participation:

Target group selection prioritizes disadvantaged populations:
- Youth with fewer opportunities: NEETs, rural residents, migrants, young unemployed from post-industrial (Silesia) and tourism-dependent (Dubrovnik) regions
- Isolated seniors: Home-bound elderly from CKM's care program, 'Google for Seniors' graduates needing continued support

Accessibility measures embedded in all activities:
- AI Voice Assistant eliminates barriers: voice-first design requires no screen reading, mouse navigation, or typing skills
- Large print materials and high-contrast visual design for all physical outputs
- Multilingual outputs (PL, HR, EN) ensuring language is not a barrier
- Training venues selected for physical accessibility (wheelchair access, proximity to public transport)
- Flexible scheduling accommodating participants with care responsibilities or health limitations

Diverse recruitment strategy:
- Partnership with local social services to reach most isolated seniors
- Outreach through existing program alumni networks ensuring trust-based recruitment
- Financial barriers removed: all participation costs covered, including transport and meals

2. ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY

Environmental responsibility integrated through green travel, digital-first approach, and conscious resource use:

Green travel commitment (target: 40% of international travel):
- Croatia-Poland route prioritizes train connections where feasible (Zagreb-Vienna-Krakow corridor)
- Bus transportation for group travel within countries
- Carbon footprint calculated and reported for all activities
- Participants receive climate impact information encouraging sustainable choices

Digital-first methodology:
- Primary outputs are digital: AI assistant, online toolkit, video tutorials
- Print materials minimized: only essential handouts for seniors without internet access
- Virtual meetings for routine coordination, reducing travel for management activities
- E-signatures for administrative documents

Sustainable event management:
- Local catering with vegetarian options at all activities
- Reusable materials: badges, folders, water bottles
- Waste sorting and recycling at all venues
- Preference for eco-certified accommodation providers

3. DIGITAL DIMENSION

Digital tools and competencies are central to DIGI-BRIDGE methodology:

Specific platforms and tools used:
- AI development: Open-source language models (Llama, Mistral), Python, FastAPI
- Collaboration: Miro for visual planning, Slack for team communication, Google Workspace for document collaboration
- Video conferencing: Zoom for virtual meetings and hybrid activities
- Learning platform: Moodle-based system hosting 20 training modules
- Assessment: DigComp self-assessment tool, Social Connection Index digital survey
- Dissemination: Canva for visual content, project website, social media presence

Digital competence development:
- Youth gain: AI literacy, pedagogical technology use, digital content creation
- Seniors gain: Basic digital skills (video calling, online services, voice assistants)
- Staff gain: AI tool integration, digital evaluation methods

Digital outputs:
- Open-source AI Voice Assistant code repository
- Online training toolkit (80 pages, 3 languages)
- Video tutorial library (20 modules)
- Digital evaluation dashboard

4. PARTICIPATION AND CIVIC ENGAGEMENT

Active citizenship and democratic participation embedded throughout project lifecycle:

Participant involvement in project governance:
- Youth Advisory Group (5 representatives) consulted on training design and AI features
- Senior Feedback Panel (5 representatives) provides input on accessibility and content priorities
- Both groups participate in mid-term evaluation and final assessment

Democratic decision-making:
- Consensus-based approach in partnership meetings
- Transparent budget allocation discussed with participant representatives
- Open feedback channels for continuous improvement

Community engagement:
- Multiplier events open to public (100 participants across both countries)
- Local stakeholder involvement: social services, libraries, community centers
- Media outreach sharing project message with wider community

European awareness building:
- Training Course includes EU citizenship module exploring Erasmus+ values
- Cross-border youth friendships demonstrate European cooperation in practice
- Project outputs credited to EU funding, raising awareness of European solidarity

FIELD 1: PLEASE PRESENT YOUR ORGANISATION (max 1000)

New Europe Foundation (NEF) is a non-governmental organization established in 2018 in Zawiercie, Silesian Voivodeship, Poland. Our mission is to bridge generations through technology and education, creating pathways for digital inclusion and active citizenship. NEF holds Erasmus+ Youth Accreditation (2024-2028), demonstrating institutional capacity for European youth projects. Our team includes Robert Klosowski (Project Manager, 20+ years EU experience, MBA, attorney), Anton Luzan (AI Developer, multilingual specialist in chatbot development and GPT integration), and Ada Grzesiuk (Coordinator, Erasmus+ applications expert). NEF operates from a dedicated office space with meeting facilities, IT infrastructure for AI development, and training rooms accessible to people with disabilities. We are registered in the National Court Register and maintain transparent financial reporting in accordance with Polish NGO regulations.

FIELD 2: WHAT ARE THE ORGANISATION'S MAIN ACTIVITIES? (max 1000)

NEF's main activities span three interconnected areas: (1) Digital Skills Development - we deliver training programs in AI literacy, digital citizenship, and technology use for various age groups, including our flagship 'Young AI Explorers' youth program and 'Google for Seniors' digital literacy course for elderly participants; (2) Intergenerational Programs - we design and implement projects connecting generations, including 'E-Senior' initiative pairing youth with elderly for mutual learning and support; (3) European Cooperation - we actively participate in Erasmus+ and other EU programs, hosting international volunteers, organizing youth exchanges, and building transnational partnerships for knowledge transfer. Additionally, NEF provides consultancy services for other organizations seeking to implement digital inclusion programs, contributing to sector capacity building in our region. Our activities reach approximately 500 direct beneficiaries annually across all programs.

FIELD 3: WHAT ARE THE ORGANISATION'S ACTIVITIES IN THE FIELD OF THIS APPLICATION? (max 1000)

In the field of intergenerational digital inclusion with AI support, NEF has developed substantial expertise through two flagship programs: (1) 'Google for Seniors' (2022-ongoing) - a digital literacy program that has successfully trained 160 seniors aged 65+ in basic digital skills including smartphone operation, video calling, and online service access. This program established our methodology for patient, accessible senior-focused digital education. (2) 'Young AI Explorers' (2024-ongoing) - a youth program introducing artificial intelligence concepts to young people aged 16-25, developing their understanding of AI ethics, practical applications, and career pathways in technology. Our AI specialist Anton Luzan has developed several chatbot prototypes and voice-enabled applications, building technical capacity for the DigiMost AI Voice Assistant proposed in this project. NEF's experience demonstrates proven ability to work with both target groups (youth and seniors) and the technical capability to develop accessible AI tools.

FIELD 4: WHAT PROFILES AND AGE GROUPS OF LEARNERS ARE CONCERNED BY THE ORGANISATION'S WORK? (max 1000)

NEF works with diverse learner profiles across the age spectrum: (1) Youth 16-29 years - particularly young people with fewer opportunities including NEETs, rural youth from Zawiercie region, and migrants participating in integration programs. Through 'Young AI Explorers' and Erasmus+ mobility projects, we engage approximately 150 young people annually. (2) Adults 30-64 years - community members seeking digital skills upgrading, parents learning alongside children, and professionals in career transition. (3) Seniors 65+ years - our primary focus for digital inclusion, particularly isolated elderly, retirees with limited technology experience, and alumni of social care programs. Through 'Google for Seniors,' we have established trusted relationships with 160 senior learners. (4) Youth workers and educators - through our Erasmus+ Accreditation activities, we train approximately 20 youth professionals annually in digital methodologies and international cooperation. Our learners share common characteristics: motivation for lifelong learning, openness to intergenerational contact, and residence in Silesian Voivodeship's smaller communities.

Our organization has implemented projects totaling over 1 million EUR, including major European Social Fund initiatives. CKM operates from accessible premises in Dubrovnik city center with training facilities, counseling rooms, and community space for intergenerational activities. We maintain strong partnerships with local government, social services, and educational institutions throughout the Dubrovnik-Neretva region and Croatian islands.

FIELD 2: WHAT ARE THE ORGANISATION'S MAIN ACTIVITIES? (max 1000)

CKM's main activities encompass: (1) Youth Career Guidance - individual counseling, group workshops, and career planning support for young people entering labor market, with special attention to those facing barriers including island youth, seasonal workers, and NEETs; (2) Intergenerational Programs - our flagship 'Za njihovu dobrobit' (For Their Well-being) initiative providing home-based support for isolated elderly through youth volunteer visits, combining practical assistance with companionship; (3) Civic Engagement - 'Youth for Society' program engaging young people in community service, democratic participation, and active citizenship; (4) International Cooperation - participation in Erasmus+ KA1 and KA2 projects, hosting volunteers through European Solidarity Corps, and building transnational partnerships. CKM has received national recognition for our intergenerational work, including awards from Croatian Ministry of Social Policy. We reach approximately 800 beneficiaries annually across all programs.

FIELD 3: WHAT ARE THE ORGANISATION'S ACTIVITIES IN THE FIELD OF THIS APPLICATION? (max 1000)

In the field of intergenerational digital inclusion, CKM brings unique expertise from 'Za njihovu dobrobit' (For Their Well-being) program - two consecutive projects (2019-2022, 2022-2025) with combined budget exceeding 1 million EUR from European Social Fund. These projects established home-based support for 120 isolated seniors in Dubrovnik area through regular youth volunteer visits. Key learnings relevant to DIGI-BRIDGE: (a) trust-based recruitment - we have established relationships with seniors who initially resist external support; (b) home-based delivery model works for those who cannot travel to center-based programs; (c) youth volunteers gain substantially from intergenerational contact, not just seniors. Additionally, our 'ACTIV8!' youth activation project has developed methodology for engaging disadvantaged youth in meaningful community service. CKM has identified digital exclusion as emerging need among our senior beneficiaries but lacks technical capacity to address it - this partnership with NEF fills that gap.

FIELD 4: WHAT PROFILES AND AGE GROUPS OF LEARNERS ARE CONCERNED BY THE ORGANISATION'S WORK? (max 1000)

CKM serves diverse populations across Dubrovnik-Neretva County: (1) Youth 15-29 years - approximately 400 young people annually through career guidance and activation programs, including NEETs, early school leavers, young unemployed from tourism-dependent economy, island community youth facing geographical barriers, and youth from minority backgrounds; (2) Seniors 65+ years - 120 beneficiaries in our 'Za njihovu dobrobit' home care database, primarily living alone, with limited family support, experiencing social isolation, and facing mobility limitations preventing participation in center-based activities; (3) Young volunteers 18-30 years - approximately 50 annually serving in our intergenerational programs, developing empathy, communication skills, and civic responsibility through direct senior contact; (4) Youth workers and social service professionals - we provide training and methodology sharing for approximately 30 professionals annually. Our learners share geographical context of Dubrovnik region: tourism seasonality affecting employment, island communities, historical emigration leaving elderly without family support, and post-war demographic challenges.

HOW THE PARTNERSHIP WAS FORMED

The DIGI-BRIDGE partnership emerged from a strategic search for complementary expertise to address an identified gap: the need to combine technological innovation with proven intergenerational care methodology.

Partner identification process:
New Europe Foundation (NEF) identified through our 'Google for Seniors' program that isolated elderly need more than one-time training - they require ongoing support, relationship-based learning, and accessible tools. However, NEF lacked established access to the most isolated seniors and proven intergenerational care models.

In 2024, NEF initiated a partner search through the Erasmus+ Partner Search platforms (SALTO, OTLAS) specifically seeking organizations with: (a) established intergenerational programs with direct senior access, (b) experience in home-based service delivery, (c) youth activation methodology, and (d) complementary geographical and cultural context.

Youth Career Center Dubrovnik (CKM) responded to our partner search, presenting their 'Za njihovu dobrobit' program as an ideal complement to NEF's digital expertise. Initial contact in October 2024 led to video conference discussions exploring mutual interests and potential synergies.

Partnership development:
- November 2024: Exchange of organizational materials and program documentation
- December 2024: Joint needs assessment identifying overlap between CKM's senior beneficiaries' digital needs and NEF's technical capacity
- January 2025: Collaborative project design session developing DIGI-BRIDGE concept
- February-March 2025: Joint application writing with clear role definition

COMPLEMENTARY STRENGTHS

NEF brings to partnership:
- AI development capacity: Staff specialist (Anton Luzan) with proven chatbot and voice assistant development experience
- Digital seniors expertise: Tested methodology from 'Google for Seniors' (160 trained)
- Technical infrastructure: Server capacity, development environment, testing facilities
- Youth digital skills programming: 'Young AI Explorers' curriculum adaptable for trainer preparation
- Project coordination experience: Erasmus+ Youth Accreditation holder with established management systems

CKM brings to partnership:
- Intergenerational care expertise: 'Za njihovu dobrobit' model developed over 6 years with over 1M EUR investment
- Direct senior access: Database of 120 isolated elderly with established trust relationships
- Home-based delivery model: Proven methodology for reaching seniors who cannot attend center-based programs
- Youth activation experience: ACTIV8! and Youth for Society programs engaging disadvantaged youth in meaningful service
- Evaluation frameworks: Robust impact assessment methods from ESF projects

WHY THIS PARTNERSHIP WORKS

Geographical complementarity:
- Poland and Croatia represent different EU membership generations (2004 vs 2013) with shared Slavic cultural context enabling smooth communication while providing sufficient diversity for transferable methodology
- Both regions face similar challenges (post-industrial/post-tourism economic transitions) but with different manifestations, allowing cross-learning

Organizational complementarity:
- NEF is technology-focused, smaller, agile organization with AI development capacity
- CKM is care-focused, larger organization with established community networks and ESF experience
- Together: technology + human touch = complete solution

Expertise complementarity:
- NEF understands digital tools but lacks care methodology and isolated senior access
- CKM understands intergenerational relationships but lacks technical innovation capacity
- Neither could develop DIGI-BRIDGE solution alone; partnership is strategic necessity, not administrative convenience

Identified risks and mitigation strategies:

1. Technical risk: AI development delays
- Mitigation: Parallel development of manual alternatives, modular design allowing partial deployment, regular technical reviews

2. Recruitment risk: Insufficient participants
- Mitigation: Early recruitment (M2-3), waiting list system, partnership with local social services
- Contingency: Extend recruitment period, expand geographical reach

3. Quality risk: Training not meeting objectives
- Mitigation: Pilot testing with small group, iterative improvement, regular participant feedback
- Contingency: Additional support sessions, one-on-one coaching

4. Partnership risk: Communication breakdown
- Mitigation: Clear roles, regular meetings, escalation procedures
- Contingency: Mediation through Project Manager, external facilitator if needed

5. External risk: Health/travel restrictions
- Mitigation: Hybrid meeting options, digital-first design, flexible scheduling
- Contingency: Full virtual delivery possible for most activities

MEASUREMENT FRAMEWORK

DIGI-BRIDGE employs comprehensive evaluation combining quantitative KPIs, qualitative assessment, and continuous monitoring to verify achievement of all project objectives.

OBJECTIVE 1: TRAIN 40 YOUTH AS DIGITAL BRIDGE TRAINERS

KPIs and measurement:

1. Completion rate - Target: 90% (36+ certified)
- Source: Training Course attendance records, certification registry
- Timing: End of Activity 2 (M11)
- Verification: Digital Bridge Trainer certificates, Youthpass completion

2. Satisfaction - Target: 80%+
- Source: Post-training survey (Likert scale 1-5)
- Timing: Final day of Training Course
- Verification: Anonymous survey, average score

3. Purpose improvement - Target: 70% increase
- Source: Pre/post Purpose in Life scale (adapted)
- Timing: Day 1 (pre) and Day 5 (post)
- Verification: Statistical comparison, percentage reporting improvement

OBJECTIVE 2: INCREASE SENIORS' DIGITAL COMPETENCE BY 50%

1. DigComp score improvement - Target: 50% average increase
- Source: DigComp self-assessment adapted for seniors (15 items)
- Timing: Week 1 (baseline) and Week 10 (endline) of Pilot Sessions
- Verification: Pre/post comparison, percentage change
- Note: DigComp is EU Digital Competence Framework, validated for adults

2. Skill mastery - Target: 85% perform 5 tasks independently
- Source: Trainer observation checklist (Week 10)
- Tasks: Video calling, health services, banking, social groups, voice assistant
- Verification: Binary yes/no per task, percentage calculation

3. Social Connection Index - Target: 40% improvement
- Source: UCLA Loneliness Scale adaptation (10 items)
- Timing: Week 1 and Week 10
- Verification: Pre/post mean score change

OBJECTIVE 3: DEPLOY AI VOICE ASSISTANT WITH 500+ INTERACTIONS

1. Interaction count - Target: 500+
- Source: AI system automatic logs
- Timing: Continuous M12-M15
- Verification: Database query, count report

2. User satisfaction - Target: 4.0/5.0
- Source: In-app feedback + exit survey
- Timing: Continuous + Week 10
- Verification: Average rating calculation

3. Usage frequency - Target: 80% weekly use
- Source: User activity logs
- Timing: Weekly during Pilot
- Verification: Active/enrolled users percentage

QUALITATIVE ASSESSMENT

- Trainer reflection journals (weekly)
- Senior testimonial interviews (10 per country)
- Focus groups (youth, seniors separately)
- Case studies (5 compelling pair stories)

DATA COLLECTION RESPONSIBILITIES

DATA MANAGEMENT

- GDPR compliance: Informed consent, anonymization, secure storage

OBJECTIVES (max 500):

DIGI-BRIDGE pursues three main objectives: (1) Train 40 young people with fewer opportunities as certified Digital Bridge Trainers equipped with skills to deliver intergenerational digital education; (2) Increase digital competence of 40 seniors aged 65+ by minimum 50% (measured via DigComp framework) through personalized sessions with youth trainers; (3) Develop and deploy 'DigiMost' AI Voice Assistant with 500+ logged interactions, providing seniors accessible 24/7 digital support. The project directly addresses the Inclusion and Diversity priority through targeting disadvantaged groups and removing participation barriers.

IMPLEMENTATION (max 500):

The project is implemented through 5 main activities over 17 months: (1) Kick-off Meeting in Dubrovnik - partnership planning and team building; (2) Training Course in Zawiercie - 5-day intensive training for 40 youth from Poland and Croatia as Digital Bridge Trainers; (3) Pilot Sessions - 10-week paired training between youth trainers and seniors in both countries; (4) AI Development - creating DigiMost voice assistant and learning platform with 20 video modules; (5) Multiplier Events in Katowice and Dubrovnik presenting results to 100 multipliers from youth work and social services sectors.

RESULTS (max 500):

Expected results include: (1) 40 certified Digital Bridge Trainers with pedagogical competencies in senior education; (2) 40 seniors with Digital Citizen certificates demonstrating mastery of 5 essential digital skills; (3) DigiMost AI Voice Assistant available as open-source tool for continued use; (4) Training Toolkit (80 pages, 3 languages) published on E+ Results Platform under CC-BY license; (5) 20 video tutorial modules on accessible learning platform; (6) 40 intergenerational relationships building social solidarity across generations; (7) Validated methodology ready for replication across Europe.
